text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
POLITICAL FRONT PAGE NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati has welcomed a deal on cooperation between Nato and Russia agreed in Moscow yesterday. However, the agreement should not limit in any way the rights of countries to play a role they deserve in international security structures, Rosati said.
- Sweden agreed to convert $6.5 million of Poland's debt, two percent of the total debt, to finance environment related schemes in Poland, according to an agreement signed in Stockholm yesterday.
ECONOMIC AND FRONT PAGE NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) will grow by 5.3 percent in 1997 and year-on-year inflation will reach 15.3 percent in December, an average index forecast by the Central and Eastern Europe Economic Research Centre (CEEERC) showed.

- Germany's Scholler-Holdings contracted the construction of three container ships in the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard. The construction, to be financed by the Polsat television president and co-owner Zygmunt Solorz, will give jobs to 2,000 workers.

- Poland's grain prices in April declined by 24.9 percent compared with the same period in 1996, while potato prices plunged by 70 percent and cattle prices went down by 3.7 percent, a report by the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The Bud-Bank construction sector bank gave up its strategy to operate as an apex bank. It will now offer financial services directly to the construction firms and seek a big strategic investor, Bud-Bank's president Jerzy Radko said.

- A banking consortium of Bank Depozytowo Kredytowy (BDK) and Pekao SA bank will extend a 157 million zloty loan to the Huta Stalowa Wola steel mill. The loan will finance modernisation and development of the plant's steel rolling line.
- Insurance firm TUiR Warta will pay a dividend of one zloty per share on July 1 to all shareholders holding Warta's stock on June 2, the company said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's president Aleksander Kwasniewski has signed the energy law act which permits competition in energy production and distribution sector.

- British Steel is mulling buying a strategic stake in the Huta Sendzimira (HTS) steel mill in Krakow, a source who declined to be named said. HTS will not provide any information on negotiations while the talks are on, the plant's spokesman Jan Berez a said.
- Poland's oldest power plant, Jaworzno 1, will be closed down on May 19 as it does not meet environmental protection norms.
- Every seventh Pole uses computers at work. Text editor and database software are the most frequently used programmes, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.

- Around 98 percent of companies in the Bydgoszcz province, central Poland, are already in private hands, the province governor Wieslaw Olszewski said. Privatisation is more effective in Bydgoszcz than in other regions of Poland, Olszewski said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's book market grows by 20 percent every year, publishers say. The 1997 book sales may exceed one billion zlotys.
- The privately-owned El-Net telecoms firm has contracted equipment and services worth $26 million from the listed Elektrim electrical engineering and foreign trade conglomerate.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland's sugar producers supported by the agriculture ministry have demanded that customs duty on sugar imports be increased because cheap sugar imports push the sugar plants into debt and will make it impossible for them to buy beet this year, the ministry said.
PARKIET
- The listed Wolczanka garment maker's sales reached 9.35 million zlotys in April, a record high in the last few years.
Reuters has not verified this stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
